reason: The arterial wall and lining look like parts of an artery, a starting point for the route through tissues.
expectation: I expect to make a lined artery; its role in the full route may become clearer afterward.

alternatives.reason: Capillaries are also needed for exchange, but I chose to start with the artery.

effect: The artery is now built, and its elastic wall stretches and recoils with the pulse. I still need the vessels that exchange materials and return blood.
reaction: The pulse and rest comparison makes the arterial wall's role clearer.
reason: Capillaries bring blood close to tissues, so I want to build that part of the route next.
expectation: I expect the lining and tiny branches to form a capillary network.

alternatives.reason: A vein is also needed for the return route, but I chose the exchange vessels first.

effect: The capillary bed is built, and its thin walls explain how materials can cross between blood and fluid around cells.
reaction: That connection between wall structure and exchange is satisfying.
reason: I want to connect the artery to the exchange vessels as the next part of the route.
expectation: I expect the arterial vessels to connect to the capillary bed; the return route will still need a vein.

effect: The artery now branches through arterioles into capillaries alongside tissue cells. The return route still needs a vein.
reaction: The parallel branches make it clear how blood reaches a broad area of tissue.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should build the vessel needed for the return route.
expectation: I expect a lined vein, though it may still need valves before joining the route.

effect: The lined vein is built; adding the valve folds is the next available step toward the return route.
reaction: The thin wall distinguishes the vein visually, though its function is not yet explained.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the folds appear to fit inside the vein.
expectation: I expect veins with valves that help prevent blood from flowing backward.

effect: The vein now has valves, and the picture shows muscle compression helping move blood toward the heart while the valves resist backflow.
reaction: The connection between muscle movement and venous return is interesting.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should connect the return vessels to the distribution and exchange route.
expectation: I expect a continuous route from arteries through capillaries to veins.

effect: The artery, capillary bed and veins now form a continuous systemic vessel network, completing the goal.
reaction: Seeing the separate vessels joined into a route is satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding valves to the veins was most worthwhile: the picture connected muscle contraction, forward blood flow and resistance to backflow.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the thin-walled veins felt least informative on its own; the picture showed their shape but did not yet explain their function.

surprise.text: The role of contracting limb muscles in helping blood return to the heart changed my understanding of venous return.

arbitrary.text: None of the combinations felt arbitrary. Several later choices were the only offered action, so they felt more like assembly than decisions.

continue.text: I would continue: connecting vessel structure to exchange and blood flow made me curious how the network will serve the rest of the body.
